A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BPP-Search and StructuredOR. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably across revisions.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original benchmark comparisons and search ablations. Tables 3–4 also report evaluations of the trained PRM and preference model.

after.justification: The original benchmark, ablation, and reward-model evaluations are retained. Tables 1–3 additionally report original analyses of StructuredOR's composition.

M1.justification: Both versions retain PRM-guided beam search, pairwise final-candidate ranking, and the same model training procedures. Equation 6's normalization correction rescales every candidate equally within a comparison and therefore preserves ranking and answer selection.

E1.justification: Both use StructuredOR, Mamo-ComplexLP, and NL4OPT. StructuredOR retains 124 examples; the newly reported industry breakdown characterizes existing coverage rather than establishing added datasets, domains, or tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same CoT variants, SC, ToT variants, and greedy/beam-search comparators. 'Randomly Greedy Search' becomes 'Random Greedy Search' without changing its participation or definition.

E3.justification: Evaluation models, test counts, solvable-subset filtering, metrics, and search configurations are unchanged. However, Figure 3 changes two dataset-generation labels from GPT-4o to GPT-4 while Section 3.2 still specifies GPT-4o; the PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a generation-setting revision or a diagram-label error.

E4.justification: New Tables 1–3 analyze dataset structure, variable instantiation, and industry composition. Existing beam-width and greedy-search ablations, manual error analysis, and appendix examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new standard deviations in Table 1 describe variation in dataset components, not uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 add descriptive results, including 1.40 abstract variables on average and 24 agriculture versus 20 logistics instances. All matched benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. PRM and preference-model results move from v1 Tables 3–4 to v3 Tables 17–18 without numerical changes.

T1.justification: Equation 6 corrects the averaging denominator from n to n−1 and makes the summation range explicit. New Appendix A.6 supplies asymptotic invocation counts for the policy, preference, and process-reward models; it adds a limited complexity analysis rather than a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The contributions remain StructuredOR's process annotations and BPP-Search's claimed accuracy and efficiency advantages. Although the abstract omits named comparators, the introduction and conclusion retain the same substantive contribution and superiority claims.

C2.justification: New Section 7 substantially expands applicability limits: computational resources restrict tree exploration, similar generated instances risk leakage and overfitting, and large numerical inputs challenge LLMs. Appendix A.6 also explains why policy-model calls dominate cost. These go beyond v1's brief computational-cost motivation and retained PRM-scoring discussion.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a StructuredOR repository address, adding concrete access information. The modeling schema, training-data construction instructions, and prompt templates in Appendices A.1–A.5 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 adds Weng (2024) and identifies reward hacking as another drawback of MCTS-based process labeling. The remaining cited works and overall positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and scattered passages receive limited editing, and the author, affiliation, and contact block changes. Section 7 and Appendices A.6–A.7 extend the document, while the existing narrative order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The revision adds three dataset tables, redraws Figures 2–4, reformats tables throughout, and moves main-text table captions below their tables. Reward-model tables relocate to the appendix. Together these substantially revise visual presentation; the appendix example images themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 improves transparency through dataset profiles, access information, explicit limitations, and a complexity analysis, while correcting Equation 6's normalization. These are useful but limited gains: empirical validation is unchanged, and Figure 3's generation-model labels conflict with the prose.
